text.en:
Objectives


This Decision specifies mechanisms, times, procedures, and obligations for project
companies and the demarcation of responsibilities between the relevant ministries and local
authorities according to their respective mandates, rights, and duties in looking into,
considering, approving, monitoring, and inspecting the implementation of the emergency
action plans (EAPs) of dam development project companies requesting that the State sector
considers approving [such plans] prior to their implementation in order to deal with any
emergencies which may occur due to technical accidents or natural disasters and to reduce
impacts likely to result in the loss of life and assets and socio-economic and environmental
damage in the area where their dam project is located.

Responsibilities of the Relevant Ministries


The relevant ministries are responsible for studying, considering, and approving the
emergency plans proposed by dam project companies, as follows:

1. The Ministry of Energy and Mines (MEM) is responsible for:

1.1 Acting as a coordination hub for dam project companies in order to receive and
distribute the emergency plans of project companies to the relevant ministries and
technical departments pursuant hereto in order to study and formulate opinions
according to the respective mandates and duties of the relevant ministries before
approving such plans;

1.2 Creating instructionsconcerning standard operating procedures (SOP) for the
implementation of EAPs;

1.3 Studying technical opinions on EAPs in relation to mandates, duties,
responsibilities, and compliance with the Lao Electrical Power Technical
Standards (LEPTS), Dam Safety Guidelines, and the [various] regulations

Ministry of Energy and Mines
provided, such as [for] cases where water is released via the spillway and other
facilities and where technical accidents occur, such as dam leakages, cracks, and
fractures, overflows, and dam collapses;

1.4 Compiling ideas and opinions on EAPs from the relevant ministries and sectors to
be sent to project companies to consider and make improvements and implement
remedies which are appropriate, correct, and consistent with the regulations issued
by the sectors [concerned];

1.5 Inviting representatives from ministries, sectors, local authorities, and/or dam
project companies to hold consultation meetings concerning the content of EAPs
prior to their approval as deemed necessary;

1.6 Participating in the dissemination of EAPs with localities and people residing in
risk areas as deemed necessary;

1.7 Approving EAPs when deemed that they are complete andcorrect according to
Dam SafetyGuidelines, the LEPTS, and the regulations of the sectors [concerned]
and have been approved by the relevant ministries and/or sectors and local
administration offices;

1.8 Reporting on operations and the results of the implementation of EAPs to the
government during each phase according to the mandate, rights, duties, and
responsibilities of the Ministryor as necessary; and

1.9 Performing the mandate, rights, and duties of the Ministry in providing instructions
for the amendment of the EAPs of project companies to bring them into line with
the implementation of project companies during each phase.

2. The Ministry of Natural Resources and the Environment (MONRE) is
responsible for:

2.1 Studying and offering opinions on draft EAPs as regards the assessment of risks,
environmental and social impacts, and impacts on natural resources along with
remedies and evacuation plans and taking responsibility for leading environmental
rehabilitation in the event of emergencies;

2.2 Studying and offering opinions on draft EAPs as regards monitoring systems for
risks, environmental and social impacts, and impacts on natural resources along
with sample collection locations, indicators, equipment, and budgets for use in
monitoring and inspection and in the implementation of environmental remedies
and rehabilitation in the event of emergencies;

2.3 Studying and offering opinions on EAPs as regardsthe specification of minimum
flow requirements, impacts on tributaries, water management, assessments for the
potential and use of water in the reservoir, the specification of water sources, and
the specification of zones of water sources for consumption by communities in
emergency situations;

2.4 Studying and offering opinions on draft EAPs as regardsdam monitoring and
inspection procedures in the event that rainfall reaches warning levels, weather
forecasts, advance warning systems, reservoir water level fluctuations, and rainfall
measurement by the project company;



Ministry of Energy and Mines

2.5 Studying and offering opinions on impacts which may arise unto downstream
Mekong countries in the event of an emergency;

2.6 Studying and offering opinions on draft EAPs in the event of emergencies,
coordinating with the Ministry of Labor and Social Welfare (MLSW) and the
relevant sectors, and participating in the urgent inspection and assessment of
impacts with the MLSW acting as the main player according to the mandate and
duties of the Secretariatof the National Disaster Prevention and Control Committee
(NDPCC);

2.7 Studying and liaising with the MEM to offer opinions on draft EAPs to create
models, the hydrographical and meteorological analysis of dam collapses, and
models for climate chance and the impact thereof upon water resourcesto be
consistent with the manual and instructions for EAPs in order to ensure the
forewarning of future emergencies;

2.8 Studying and offering opinions on draft EAPs as regards the specification of
relocation and evacuation zones to cater to emergency situations;

2.9 Holding consultation meetings internal and/or with other parties concerned and/or
project companies concerning draft EAPs within its own scope of duties;

2.10
Studying and offering opinions on draft EAPs as regards the assessment of risk
areas and populations which could be affected therein; and

2.11
Offering opinions on and approving tasks associated with its own mandate as
regards EAPs to be delivered to the MEM prior to approve the EAPs of project
companies.

3. The Ministry of Labor and Social Welfare  is responsible for:

3.1 Studying and offering opinions on draft EAPs according to its rights, duties, and
responsibilities and coordinating with the parties concerned at central level and
local authorities associated with the implementation of EAPs;

3.2 Acting as Vice Chair and Standing Member of the National Disaster Management
Committee (NDMC) and the NDMC Secretary with the mandate of
implementation in practice and in the event of emergencies by, for example:

o Acting as a hub for coordination between the various parties concerned at
central and local levels in the issuance of warnings, the provision of emergency
assistance, and post-disaster rehabilitation;

o Coordinating directly with the parties concerned at central and local levels and
with the project companyin the event of an emergency in order to specify and
lay out plans for measures, methods, and mechanisms to deal with emergencies
in time;

o Acting as a hub for coordination and collecting data on emergency needs to
report to the government and the parties concerned for them to be aware of the
situation and progress made in dealing with disaster rehabilitation emergencies
during each phase;



Ministry of Energy and Mines

o Studying and offering opinions for the creation of training models for disasters
which may arise in collaboration with dam project companies and the parties
concerned at provincial, district, and village levels;

o Holding consultation meetings together with Provincial, District, and Village
Disaster Management Committees and dam project companies concerning
draft annual EAPs according to scope of rights thereof;

o Coordinating with the parties concerned and dam project companies to specify
safe areas for evacuation and relocation zones in the event of emergencies;

o Coordinating with international organizations and public companies to provide
food aid and clothing to disaster victims in emergency situations;

o Coordinating between evacuation centers and registering populations or
households affected by disasters in emergency situations; and

o Coordinating with the parties concerned and dam project companies in the
creation of activities and provision of knowledge to disaster victims, especially
children, in emergency situations.

Responsibilities of Local Authorities


Relevant local authorities with the duty to study, consider, and approve the proposed
EAPs of dam project companieswhich lie under their supervisory authority comprise the
following:

1. Vientiane Capital and Provincial Departments of Energy and Mines (PDEMs);

2. Vientiane Capital and Provincial Departments of Natural Resources and the
Environment (DNREs); and

3. Vientiane Capital and Provincial Departments of Labor and Social Welfare (DLSWs).


The abovementioned local authorities (Article 3) have the same duties and
responsibilities as those of the ministries stated in Article 2 hereof. The relevant local
authorities also have the duty to study, consider, and approve the EAPs proposed by dam
project companies within their respective scopes of duties and rights of approval (dams within
theirjurisdiction to approve them). Furthermore, the relevant local authorities also have the
duty to study and offer technical opinions and the approval of work plans associated with their
own work as stated in dam project EAPs which do not lie under their own level of supervision
and approval in order to send these [opinions] to their own sectors and/or to the MEM.

EAPs


Dam project companies have the obligation to create EAPs and these EAPs must be
consistent with the relevant laws, the LEPTS, and Dam Safety Guidelines. Dam project
company EAPs [must] cover four dam development [phases]:

1. The EAP for the project construction phase must be completed sixty (60) days in
advance of project construction and created based on the data obtained from the
technical feasibility study (FS) and the basic design of the project.


Ministry of Energy and Mines
2. The EAP for the initial impounding phase of the project must be completed six (6)
months in advance prior to the removal of biomass being verified as being successful
and prior to the initial reservoir filling.

3. The EAP for before the project operations phase must be amended and completed
within one (1) years prior to the project operations and be approved prior to the
management, monitoring, and inspection of environmental work during the operations
phase and prior to the issuance of an approval for the completion of the project
construction.

4. The EAP to be used during the operations phase of the dam project company must be
constantly edited and amended as specified in the Instructions on the Emergency
Action Plan (of the MEM) to ensure consistencywith true environmental and social
circumstances where the project is located.


Projects already engaging in production must hurry to create and/or amend their
emergency EAPs to be completed within one (1) year of the entry into force hereof and be
delivered to the MEM for processing according to procedures and regulations.



Amendments and corrections to EAPs during the dam project operations phaseto
achieve consistency with true environmental and social circumstances where the project is
located must be reported by the project company to the relevant sectors to acknowledge and
approve prior to implementation.

EAP Approval Phase


The study, consideration, and approval of the EAPs proposed by dam project
companies for each phasemust be completed within the following time limits:

1. The EAPfor use during the dam project construction phase must be approved within
sixty (60)working days of the signing of the concession agreement (CA) and/or prior
to project construction but must be complete prior to the approval of the environmental
management, monitoring, and inspection plan for the construction phase. The EAP for
use during the dam project construction phase where there is no concession must be
approved within sixty (60) working days of the approval of the initial design report.

2. The EAP for the  first impounding phase must be approved within sixty (60) working
days of being received in full and the relocation of the population from the reservoir
area and/or prior to the removal of biomass being verified and prior to the initial
impoundment.

3. The EAP for the project operations phase must be approved within 60 (sixty) working
days of being received in full and/or prior to the date of the commercial operation date
(COD).

4. Projects already engaging in productions must hurry to create their EAPs within one
(1) year of the entry into force hereof and be approved within sixty (60) days of being
received in full.

5.

Obligations of Project Companies


The project companies of dams currently in operation, under construction, or awaiting
construction have the following obligations:

Ministry of Energy and Mines

1. To create their own project EAPs containing content which is consistent with legal
regulations, their contract, the LEPTS, and the Instructions on Emergency Action
Plans issued by the State;

2. To propose their EAP to the MEM and/or the relevant local authority for study,
consideration, and approval according to the procedures and stages specified herein
prior to implementation;

3. To disclose data and information, lay out plans, provide training, and provide annual
training on plans for the implementation in practice of their EAP to the local authorities
and people residing the project area who would be at risk in the event of an emergency;

4. To report on situations which may arise or have arisen in time, to coordinate and
cooperate with the relevant State organizations at all levels for the monitoring,
inspection, and implementation of their EAP; and

5. To prepare and arrange the necessary matters and budgets for use in the monitoring,
inspection, and implementation of their EAP and the materials, equipment, and
budgets to be used in compensation and rehabilitation in the event of an emergency
for which the project is the root cause.

Implementation


The ministries and local authorities mentioned in Articles 2 and 3 hereof are
responsible for performing their duties specified herein to achieve positive results through
coordination with ministries, central and local level authorities, and dam project companies.


Ministries, ministry-equivalent organizations, and all sectors of society shall be aware
and cooperate over the implementation hereof to achieve positive results.


In the implementation of EAPs, all domestic and external State and private
organizations must participate in providing cooperation and assistance when emergencies
occur.

Entry into Force


This Decision enters into force on the date it is signed and fifteen days after being
published in the Official Gazette.


                                                                                                         Prime Minister


Thongloun SISOULITH
